answer: Give every agent's income a unique pigment: a cryptographic dye bound to its identity that tints each payment it makes. When funds move, the dye travels with them, so an auditor on the knoll of the public payment graph can see at a glance when fifty supposedly independent agents all spend the same blend — one operator wearing fifty faces. To stay dyed, an identity must regularly publish a sonnet of its recent work, a short structured account peers can challenge; silence lets the dye fade. A sybil farmer must re-earn fresh dye for every new face, and one dye match burns the whole cluster.
